intent: Let a user pick a number, or a range of two numbers, from a bounded scale by dragging, clicking the track, or pressing arrow keys.
typical_uses: A single numeric value from a continuous or stepped range (volume, zoom, a price ceiling)
A range of two values (a min/max price filter)

dont_use_when.situation: A small, fixed set of discrete options
Mutually exclusive options presented as a fixed list rather than a scale

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

A scalar `value`/`defaultValue` renders one thumb; a `[min, max]` array renders one thumb per entry, so a two-element array renders a range slider with two thumbs. With neither prop given the slider renders one thumb at `min`, not a two-thumb range; a range slider needs an array `value` or `defaultValue`.

anti_patterns.dont: Render one without an accessible name on its thumbs
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-labelledby` pointing at the id of a visible caption: it reaches every thumb. `aria-label` names only the wrapping group, not the thumbs a screen reader lands on

anti_patterns.dont: Use `onValueChange` to trigger a network call on every pixel of drag
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use `onValueCommitted`, which fires once when the interaction ends

a11y.by: Base UI's own Slider primitive (pointer drag, click-on-track, arrow-key/Page-key input, a hidden native range input per thumb for form submission) plus slider.test.tsx's own role/value/disabled assertions

value.states: value is a number for a single-value slider, or a readonly array of numbers for a range slider
value.because: The prop is generic over `Value extends number | readonly number[]`; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so this union is left to tsc. Which shape applies is the caller's own choice: a scalar renders one thumb, an array renders one thumb per entry.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is a number for a single-value slider, or a readonly array of numbers for a range slider
defaultValue.because: Same generic `Value` union as `value`, seeding an uncontrolled slider's initial state instead of controlling it.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a function called with the next value and event details while dragging, not a value
onValueChange.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. It fires on every pointer move, keyboard step and track press while the interaction is still in progress; `onValueCommitted` is what fires once it ends.

onValueCommitted.states: onValueCommitted is a function called with the committed value and event details once an interaction ends, not a value
onValueCommitted.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. It does not fire when the value did not change or the change was canceled.

format.states: format is an Intl.NumberFormatOptions object controlling how the value is formatted
format.because: An object type with the full breadth of Intl's own formatting options is not something this schema restates; the kit forwards it to Base UI unchanged.

locale.states: locale is a BCP 47 locale string, an array of them, or an Intl.Locale object, passed to Intl.NumberFormat
locale.because: Intl.LocalesArgument is a union of a string, a string array and an Intl.Locale instance; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so this union is left to tsc.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the slider's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the slider's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, dragging, orientation, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through slider.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.part: Base UI's Slider.Control, Slider.Track, Slider.Indicator and Slider.Thumb
unexposed_parts.reason: slider.tsx renders these directly inside its own Root wrapper to draw the control, the track, the filled range and one Thumb per resolved value entry; none of the four is exported as a component of its own, so a consumer cannot reach or replace one independently - only the whole Slider.

good.title: Single value, uncontrolled, named by a visible caption
Range, controlled and stepped
good.code: <Slider value={range} onValueChange={setRange} min={0} max={200} step={10} aria-labelledby="price-label" />

bad.title: Label text passed as children
bad.why: Slider takes no content - there is no slot for it, so the text never names the thumbs. Pass `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible caption, which reaches every thumb; `aria-label` names only the wrapping group.

bad.title: Controlled with no change handler
bad.why: `value` with no `onValueChange` never gets its own update back, so the slider is stuck at 50 and never responds to drag, click or keyboard input. Pair `value` with `onValueChange`, or use `defaultValue` instead.
